title: Tavil (barrel drum)
summary: The tavil is the big barrel drum of south Indian processions and concerts. Struck on one head with a stick and on the other with the fingers, it answers the long double-reed pipe with sharp, ringing strokes, and a thick leather ring and broad straps hold the skin tight. Here it is seen from the stick side.
howToPlay: The drum faces you: the black paste at the middle of the skin, the leather ring round it and the straps fanning out behind.
Paste is the middle, Open the ring round it, Slap the outer skin, Rim the hoop and Leather the straps.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Strike as it lands.
Begin with the open strokes, then add the slap and the rim.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The patterns count four beats to the bar.
heritageNote: A tavil player is trained to answer the pipe phrase for phrase. The drummer listens to each line of the melody and replies with a rhythm built from the same number of beats, so the two instruments seem to talk to each other.
credits: Tradition: the தவில்; patterns written for this game
